intro: Data entry keyers work fast and accurately with records. The closest of the 25 careers below is File Clerks, with a 93% skill match, while title examiners are 85% matched and earn a BLS May 2025 median of $58,650, which is 42% more than the $41,340 data entry keyers earn.
why_it_works: Keying data means working through large volumes, catching errors and meeting daily quotas without losing focus. O*NET rates time management at 3 out of 5 for this job and complex problem solving at 2.88. Billing, payroll, title and postal clerk jobs use the same accuracy. All of the top 10 matches pay more. The skills to build are operations analysis and troubleshooting.
tips: Payroll and Timekeeping Clerks earn $58,260, which is 41% more, often after a short certificate.
Production, Planning, and Expediting Clerks earn $59,650, or 44% more, and value data accuracy.
Learn spreadsheet formulas and reporting; analysis is your most common skill gap.

faq.q: What jobs can former data entry keyers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are File Clerks (93%), billing and posting clerks (87%) and title examiners and searchers (85%), based on O*NET 31.0. Correspondence Clerks are 85% matched and earn $46,800, which is 13% more than the $41,340 data entry median.

faq.q: Which careers for data entry keyers pay more?
faq.a: 21 of the 25 matches pay more. Postal Service Clerks earn $62,130 (50% more), production and expediting clerks $59,650 (44% more) and title examiners $58,650 (42% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. All three train new workers on the job.

faq.q: Do data entry keyers need more education to switch?
faq.a: Usually not. 20 of the 25 matches need no more education than data entry keyers already have, including 7 of the top 10. In the closest match, 38% of workers have an associate degree, though many employers hire without one.

faq.q: What skills should data entry keyers learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are operations analysis, troubleshooting, judgment and decision making and operation and control. Coordination already rates 2.75 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so analyzing records and fixing problems are the main steps up.
